correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary scalar shift of the Jordan operator, the bracket changes by c(alpha*y-beta*x), which belongs to each tested subalgebra and to the sum of two subalgebras. Every subalgebra is either an arbitrary subspace of the abelian ideal or one of q^(r-j) affine lifts of the unique J-invariant j-space. Mixed permutability is exactly the condition U+W_j=W_l, counted by a Gaussian coefficient and a quotient graph; outside/outside permutability is exactly b-a in W_(max(j,k)+1), giving the stated polynomial. The asymptotic limits follow from leading Gaussian powers and precise dominant type densities. The independent RREF enumerator verifies seven small prime-field pairs, plus scalar shift invariance of complete pair graphs at ranks two and three. The characteristic and quantifier boundaries are explicit; no finite experiment is elevated to universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact all-rank two-subalgebra incidence statistic for the natural Jordan-chain/standard filiform semidirect family gives a sharp field-growth threshold: almost no pairs permute at lengths two and three, exactly one quarter asymptotically at length four, and almost all at length at least five. The scalar-shift connection shows the phenomenon spans nilpotent and nonnilpotent Lie algebras with the same complete subalgebra pair relation. The previously known rank-three special case is credited; the mathematical value is the new full-rank count and structural phase transition, not the recovery of a historical small-rank polynomial.
